cases.sentence: ___ у меня к этому моменту как раз образовалась
cases.translation: I had just started a family by that point.
cases.explain: Семья is the grammatical subject of образовалась (had formed), so it is Nominative.

cases.sentence: Подать документы в ЗАГС надо было за два месяца до ___
cases.translation: We had to file the paperwork at the registry office two months before the wedding.
cases.explain: The preposition до governs the Genitive case.

cases.translation: I was eventually expelled from the Yabloko party.
cases.explain: The preposition из governs the Genitive case.

cases.sentence: Явлинский лично позвонил ___ и велел меня заретушировать
cases.translation: Yavlinsky personally called the designer and ordered him to airbrush me out.
cases.explain: The verb позвонить (to call someone) governs the Dative case.

cases.sentence: она, смеясь, признавалась мне, что, конечно, прокручивала в голове эту ___ много раз и думала, как отреагировать
cases.translation: She admitted to me, laughing, that of course she had played out that scene in her head many times and thought about how to react.
cases.explain: Сцену is the direct object of прокручивала (was replaying), so it is Accusative.

cases.sentence: раздали на заседании Политбюро партии, чтобы обосновать мое ___
cases.translation: ...they handed out at the Politburo meeting to justify my expulsion.
cases.explain: Исключение is the direct object of обосновать (to justify); for this neuter noun the Accusative matches the Nominative.

cases.sentence: Мы с Юлей хотели детей, и я очень обрадовался, когда стал ___
cases.translation: Yulia and I wanted children, and I was overjoyed when I became a father.
cases.explain: A predicate noun after стать (to become) takes the Instrumental case.

cases.sentence: У меня в ___ висит фотография Сальвеевского конгресса физиков
cases.translation: In my office hangs a photograph of the Solvay Congress of physicists.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the Prepositional case.

reading.ru: В 1999 году, когда Путин только пришел к власти, многие были от него в восторге.
reading.question: How did many people initially feel about Putin when he first came to power in 1999?
reading.correct: They were thrilled/enthusiastic
reading.explain: The text says many people were thrilled with him when he first came to power.

reading.ru: Коммунисты по-прежнему были крупнейшей организацией и очевидным решением для человека, который хотел заявить о своей оппозиции преемнику Ельцина.
reading.question: Which party was the "obvious" choice for someone wanting to oppose Yeltsin's successor, given its size?
reading.correct: The Communists
reading.explain: The Communists were still the largest organization and the obvious choice for anyone opposing Yeltsin's successor.

reading.ru: Я хотел ясно обозначить свою позицию и с принципа «пойти и вступить», и я отправился в офис «Яблоко» на Новом Арбате.
reading.question: Where was the Yabloko office Navalny went to join the party?
reading.correct: On Novy Arbat
reading.explain: He went to the Yabloko office on Novy Arbat.

reading.ru: Они глядели на меня с подозрением и все спрашивали.
reading.question: How did the local Yabloko members react when Navalny said he wanted to join?
options: They looked at him with suspicion
They asked him to lead the branch immediately
reading.correct: They looked at him with suspicion
reading.explain: The text says they looked at him with suspicion and kept asking questions.

reading.ru: Большинство людей вступало в яблоко из личной симпатии к Григорию Явлинскому.
reading.question: Why did most people join Yabloko, according to Navalny?
options: Out of personal sympathy for Grigory Yavlinsky
Because it was the ruling party
reading.correct: Out of personal sympathy for Grigory Yavlinsky
reading.explain: Most people joined Yabloko out of personal sympathy for Grigory Yavlinsky.

reading.ru: Я сто раз слышал, что денег совсем нет или почти нет.
reading.question: What did Navalny repeatedly hear about Yabloko's finances?
options: That there was little or no money
That the party was extremely wealthy
That funding was a state secret
reading.correct: That there was little or no money
reading.explain: He says he heard a hundred times that there was no money, or almost none.

reading.ru: Начав ими заниматься и поработав наблюдателем на выборах, я сразу понял две вещи.
reading.question: What experience led Navalny to two realizations about his legal skills and elections?
reading.correct: Working as an election observer
reading.explain: After starting to work on elections and serving as an observer, he immediately realized two things.

reading.ru: В новый 2000 год, который мы с Юлей отмечали вдвоем, я сделал ей предложение.
reading.question: When did Navalny propose to Yulia?
options: On New Year's Eve 2000, while celebrating alone with her
During a work trip to Kirov
reading.correct: On New Year's Eve 2000, while celebrating alone with her
reading.explain: He proposed on New Year's Eve 2000, which they were celebrating just the two of them.

reading.ru: Накануне Юля отравилась.
reading.question: What happened to Yulia the night before they needed to file their marriage documents?
options: She got into a car accident
She fell asleep and missed the appointment
reading.correct: She got food poisoning
reading.explain: The text says Yulia got food poisoning the night before.

reading.ru: В 2001 году родилась наша дочка Даша.
reading.question: In what year was Navalny's daughter Dasha born?
reading.explain: The text states their daughter Dasha was born in 2001.

reading.ru: На них я возглавил московский штаб и начал организовывать разные мероприятия совместно с молодежным крылом «Яблоко», которым руководил Илья Яшин.
reading.question: What role did Navalny take on during the 2003 Duma elections?
options: Head of the Moscow campaign headquarters
reading.correct: Head of the Moscow campaign headquarters
reading.explain: He headed the Moscow campaign headquarters during the 2003 elections.

reading.ru: Количество голосов дошло до 4,3%, но больше не увеличивалось.
reading.question: What percentage of the vote did Yabloko's count reach on election night, before stalling?
reading.explain: The vote count reached 4.3% and stopped rising there.

reading.ru: В 2016 году, когда Яблоко в очередной раз избиралась в дому, вышла реклама с Явленским.
reading.question: What kind of ad featuring Yavlinsky came out during Yabloko's 2016 Duma campaign?
options: One where he sat in a dark room revealing signs with phrases
reading.correct: One where he sat in a dark room revealing signs with phrases
reading.explain: In the ad he sat in a dark room holding white placards with phrases, revealed one by one.

reading.ru: Тогда, в 2016 году, на выборах в Думу партия Яблоко набрала 1,99%.
reading.question: What percentage did Yabloko get in the 2016 Duma elections?
reading.explain: The text states Yabloko got 1.99% in the 2016 elections.

reading.ru: Из партии «Яблоко» меня в итоге исключили.
reading.question: What ultimately happened to Navalny's membership in Yabloko?
options: He was expelled from the party
He was promoted to party chairman
He was elected as deputy chairman
reading.correct: He was expelled from the party
reading.explain: The text directly states he was ultimately expelled from the Yabloko party.

reading.ru: Эти акции, как правило, разрешали проводить только на окраине города, и даже там на них собиралось несколько тысяч человек.
reading.question: Where were the nationalist "Russian marches" typically permitted to take place?
options: Only on the outskirts of the city
In the very center of Moscow
They were never permitted at all
reading.correct: Only on the outskirts of the city
reading.explain: The marches were usually only allowed on the outskirts of the city, yet still drew several thousand people.

reading.ru: Я могу разговаривать с демократами, потому что я сам один из них.
reading.question: Why does Navalny say he can talk with democrats?
options: Because he is a democrat himself
Because he was trained as a diplomat
Because they pay him to consult
Because he fears their criticism otherwise
reading.correct: Because he is a democrat himself
reading.explain: He says he can talk with democrats because he is one of them himself.

reading.ru: В «Яблоке» этим быстро воспользовались и в 2006-м решили исключить меня из партии под предлогом участия в русском марше.
reading.question: What official pretext did Yabloko use to expel Navalny in 2006?
options: His participation in a Russian March
reading.correct: His participation in a Russian March
reading.explain: Yabloko used his participation in a Russian March as the pretext to expel him in 2006.

reading.ru: Как рассказали Яшину, Явлинский лично позвонил дизайнеру и велел меня заретушировать.
reading.question: What did Yavlinsky allegedly personally order regarding a newspaper photo of Navalny?
options: He told the designer to airbrush Navalny out of it
He asked for the photo to be enlarged
He requested Navalny be given a byline
reading.correct: He told the designer to airbrush Navalny out of it
reading.explain: As Yashin was told, Yavlinsky personally called the designer and ordered Navalny be airbrushed out of the photo.

reading.ru: Напоследок я произнес пылкую речь, и на этом с моей работой в «Яблоке» было покончено.
reading.question: How did Navalny's time working for Yabloko formally end?
options: He gave a passionate speech, and that was the end of his work there
He was escorted out by security without a word
He was reinstated after an appeal
reading.correct: He gave a passionate speech, and that was the end of his work there
reading.explain: He delivered a passionate speech, and with that his work at Yabloko was over.

reading.ru: Я познакомился там с разными хорошими людьми, например, с Петром Уфицеровым, с которым нам придется многое пройти вместе, но тогда мы об этом не подозревали.
reading.question: Who did Navalny meet at Yabloko whom he would later go through a lot with?
reading.correct: Pyotr Ofitserov
reading.explain: He mentions meeting Pyotr Ofitserov there, with whom he would later go through a great deal.

reading.ru: Я и мои коллеги были основателями фактически главной и самой успешной правозащитной организации Москвы – Комитета защиты москвичей.
reading.question: What organization does Navalny say he and his colleagues founded?
options: The Committee for the Defense of Muscovites, a human rights organization
reading.correct: The Committee for the Defense of Muscovites, a human rights organization
reading.explain: He says he and his colleagues founded Moscow's leading human rights organization, the Committee for the Defense of Muscovites.

reading.ru: Пример – недавний опыт Югославии, где дикий, безумный, тоталитарный национализм Милошевича был сокрушен не жалкой либеральной оппозицией, а национально-демократическим движением Каштуницы, получившим массовую поддержку избирателей.
reading.question: What example from Yugoslavia does Navalny cite in his speech to support his argument?
options: Milosevic's nationalism being defeated by a national-democratic movement, not liberal opposition
A liberal coalition overthrowing a monarchy
reading.correct: Milosevic's nationalism being defeated by a national-democratic movement, not liberal opposition
reading.explain: He cites Yugoslavia, where Milosevic's nationalism was crushed by Kostunica's national-democratic movement, not the liberal opposition.

reading.ru: Мы уже проходили это в 2003 году, когда было заявлено, что наш параллельный пересчет показал, что мы преодолели 5%.
reading.question: What false claim from 2003 does Navalny say Yabloko had already made once before?
options: That their parallel recount showed they'd crossed the 5% threshold
That they had won a majority in parliament
That international observers certified their win
That Yavlinsky had been elected president
reading.correct: That their parallel recount showed they'd crossed the 5% threshold
reading.explain: He recalls that in 2003 it was claimed their parallel recount showed they had passed the 5% barrier, which was untrue.

reading.ru: И первое решение, которого я требую как член Федерального Совета партии, избранной московской организацией, немедленная отставка председателя партии и всех его заместителей.
reading.question: What immediate demand did Navalny make in his farewell speech?
options: The immediate resignation of the party chairman and all his deputies
A public apology to him personally
His own reinstatement in the party
reading.correct: The immediate resignation of the party chairman and all his deputies
reading.explain: He demanded, as a member of the party's Federal Council, the immediate resignation of the party chairman and all his deputies.
